investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — no new remote-agent pod can be placed. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful). This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the two eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/stuck pods have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three sibling checks reporting the same Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 of 6 nodes are even eligible for remote-agent pods. If those two nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is blocked. This may reflect a cluster topology that is undersized for the current load.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their pods, those pods may be occupying VM resource slots without doing useful work, starving new scheduling attempts.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource shows available capacity on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and the cause would shift to a misconfigured resource request or quota.

If a subsequent eval run with the same cluster state succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent usage) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If the four affinity-mismatched nodes are shown to have been recently reconfigured or tainted to exclude remote-agent pods, the root cause would shift to a node configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the runner is shown to have submitted pods with an incorrect resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more slots than any single node can provide), the cause would be a probe configuration error rather than cluster-level exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct signal rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that counts Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 5 minutes) to detect leaked or zombie pods before they exhaust the VM resource pool.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 nodes), alerting on topology shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Consider a latency-banded eval that warns when remote-agent pod scheduling exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 60s) before the current 129s hard failure, providing earlier signal of capacity pressure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never produced a schedulable pod, so no agent identity was established and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available for scheduling and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod is rejected as Unschedulable. Because pod creation never succeeds, the eval runner cannot obtain an agentId or poll agent state, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (requiring orgId, agentId, readyState, state) receives zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity, leaving no schedulable target.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion would produce exactly this failure pattern across all three sibling checks.

Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run consuming VM slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in the runner) failed on a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and blocking new scheduling.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-18 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims eligible, every remote-agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~129–152 s each), preventing agent creation and all downstream eval steps. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint, not an application code defect. No suspect code changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to implicate a software regression.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — no new remote-agent pod can be placed. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful). This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not an application code defect. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent or recently created remote-agent pods have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval probe pods.
[Likely] A prior eval run or user-initiated remote agent was not cleaned up and is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, preventing new pods from scheduling.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity; if the affinity were broadened or more kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.
[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit range at the namespace level was reduced, lowering the effective ceiling without changing node hardware.
[Low likelihood] A transient cluster event (node NotReady, node drain, resource pressure eviction) temporarily reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool (production cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that carry this resource type, indicating pool exhaustion (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).
affectedAreas.details: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded entirely by node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure on the 2 kata-capable nodes.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling / node affinity configuration
affectedAreas.reason: The pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict placement to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. This configuration, combined with resource exhaustion, makes preemption impossible (evidence: failed-check.message).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to confirm pool exhaustion and quantify the shortfall.
Audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations; terminate any leaked, completed, or orphaned remote-agent pods that are not actively serving user traffic.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any cleanup to determine whether capacity is restored and scheduling succeeds.

If exhaustion is confirmed as persistent (not just from leaked pods), evaluate increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on existing nodes or adding additional kata-capable nodes to the cluster.
Review whether the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods can be safely broadened to include additional nodes, reducing the blast radius of future capacity events on the 2 kata-capable nodes.

Note that remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are registered as required=true (infra/evals/status/features.json line 183–184); with degradedAfterFailures=1, the remote-agents feature is already in degraded state. Confirm the feature health status dashboard reflects this correctly.

This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production Kubernetes cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; do not escalate as a confirmed user-facing outage until cluster telemetry or user reports corroborate impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would be ruled out as the cause.
If the pod's node affinity/selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., pointing to a non-existent label), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a configuration error.

If a subsequent eval run with no other remote-agent pods running also produced the Unschedulable message, it would suggest the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit is set too low for even a single probe pod, pointing to a quota misconfiguration rather than contention.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passed on a re-run shortly after this failure without any infrastructure changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike (e.g., a concurrent load test or user burst) rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the shared scheduling root cause would be disproved and a check-specific issue would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for pod scheduling timeout.
Add a remote-agent pod leak detection eval that alerts when remote-agent pods remain in Running or Pending state beyond a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) without an active eval run owning them.

Add a node affinity/selector validation eval that confirms at least N kata-capable nodes with sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm headroom exist before the remote-agents eval suite runs, surfacing capacity risk proactively.

Consider a synthetic canary eval that requests a minimal kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation on a schedule shorter than the current staleAfterMinutes=20 window, providing earlier warning of capacity exhaustion before full remote-agent checks are attempted.
